summary: Saudi Arabia procures solar and wind through the Saudi Power Procurement Company under its National Renewable Energy Program, with the sovereign fund PIF financing about 70% of the target capacity. Self-consumption rules cover solar and wind, and money can move freely, but the legal framework lags behind commercial activity.

access.reason: SPPC procures solar and wind rounds under the National Renewable Energy Program, with 1.3 GW of solar closing in 2023.

ownership.reason: There is no limit on moving profits, capital or debt service in or out, apart from withholding taxes.

stability.reason: The government aims for 50% renewable electricity by 2030, but the legal framework may lag behind commercial developments.

direction.reason: Spending on power and renewables is expected to reach $293 billion by 2030.

access.reason: The 2022 self-consumption framework covers solar and wind for consumers, building on 2020 rules for systems of 1 kW to 2 MW.

ownership.reason: No limits on moving profits or capital.

build.reason: Each offtaker may connect up to 5 MW under the small-scale framework.
